correctness.rationale: Exact distance formulas classify every scale-two clique into P, C_i, D_ij, or T_ijk. The subcomplex generated by P, C_i, and D_ij is contractible because subdivision vertices can be deleted sequentially with contractible links. The remaining \(\binom n3\) triangular 2-cells attach along full boundaries, yielding a wedge of \(\binom n3\) two-spheres. Scale one is a connected graph of cycle rank \(\binom{n-1}{2}\), and scale three is a cone. A standalone exact GF(2) computation reconstructs and checks \(3\le n\le7\).

value.rationale: \(S(K_n)\) is a canonical infinite incidence/subdivision family. The result gives its entire positive-dimensional graph-metric Rips barcode in closed form and explains a sharp one-dimensional-to-two-dimensional transition by a contractible core with one essential triangle per original vertex triple. Contractibility at scale three occurs before the diameter-four full-simplex threshold for \(n\ge4\), so the result is more than a restatement of diameter.
